title: What does a knowledge web commit us to?
subtitle: Architecture, participation, and evolutionary philosophy
summary: An editorial route through seven existing records, asking what was proposed, what was implemented, whose meanings are retained, and which values guide the programme. It asserts no historical influence.
audience: readers evaluating a knowledge network or an evolutionary argument

steps.heading: What is the project trying to build?
steps.narrative: Separate the collaborative undertaking and its philosophical commitments from its publishing medium.

steps.heading: What was implemented?
steps.narrative: Read the dated technical admissions alongside the proposed features; no present annotation service was tested.

steps.heading: What does a typed link assert?
steps.narrative: Distinguish a proposed relation system, actual implementation, and a reader interpretation.

steps.heading: Whose definition is this?
steps.narrative: Keep the constituent glossary authors visible; this pass covers the introductory index, not all entries.

steps.heading: What new control appears?
steps.narrative: Identify the controlling mechanism. A larger aggregate alone does not establish a transition.

steps.heading: Which kind of claim is being made?
steps.narrative: Distinguish a transition definition from the wider philosophy, historical interpretations, forecasts, and ethics.

steps.heading: Which values enter the programme?
steps.narrative: Examine attributed commitments and domain-specific evidence without treating the programme as field consensus.
